items.stem: In a materials metrology audit, a machined titanium-aluminide reference cube records a mass of 59.4 g ± 1.2 g on a digital balance and an edge length of 3 cm ± 0.04 cm using vernier callipers. What is the bulk density of the cube expressed in coherent SI base units (kg m⁻³)?
items.workedSolution: Convert to SI base units: m = 59.4 × 10⁻³ = 0.0594 kg and L = 3 × 10⁻² = 0.03 m. Volume V = L³ = (0.03)³ m³. Bulk density ρ = m / L³ = 2.20 × 10³ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Converts mass to kg and cubed edge length to m³ to obtain ρ = 2.20 × 10³ kg m⁻³.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates density in g cm⁻³ without applying the factor of 1000 needed to convert g cm⁻³ into kg m⁻³.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass in kilograms by a single edge length in metres instead of cubing the converted length.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Applies the centimetre prefix 10⁻² once rather than cubing it to (10⁻²)³ = 10⁻⁶ when converting cm³ to m³.

items.stem: During quality inspection of a syntactic-foam subsea buoyancy block, a technician measures the cubic specimen to have edge length 3.2 cm ± 0.04 cm and mass 147 g ± 1.5 g. What is the percentage uncertainty in the calculated density of the cube?
items.workedSolution: Since ρ = m L⁻³, Δρ / ρ = Δm / m + 3(ΔL / L) = (1.5/147) + 3(0.04/3.2). Expressing as a percentage gives 4.77%.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the percentage uncertainty in edge length once instead of multiplying it by the power exponent 3 for L³.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts percentage uncertainties in the quotient m / L³ instead of adding worst-case contributions.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Cubes the percentage uncertainty in L rather than multiplying the fractional uncertainty by 3.

items.stem: A solid-state laboratory prepares a cubic silicon-carbide ceramic billet of measured mass 256 g ± 2 g; micrometric gauging gives each side of the cube as 3.2 cm ± 0.06 cm. What is the absolute uncertainty Δρ in the density when expressed in kg m⁻³?

markScheme.criterion: Combines SI density with fractional uncertainty Δm/m + 3ΔL/L to obtain Δρ = 500 kg m⁻³.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of 3 from L³ when propagating the fractional uncertainty of the edge length.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Leaves the absolute uncertainty in g cm⁻³ rather than converting to kg m⁻³.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the fractional uncertainty of L³ from that of mass in the quotient m / L³.

items.stem: By dimensional homogeneity, the transverse wave speed v along a taut cable depends only on tension T (in N, i.e. kg m s⁻²) and linear mass density μ (mass per unit length) via v = Tᵃ μᵇ with dimensionless constant equal to unity. In an acoustic wire rig, T = 48 N ± 1.2 N and μ = 3 g m⁻¹ ± 0.1 g m⁻¹. Deduce the exponents a and b by dimensional homogeneity and calculate the wave speed v in m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: Matching SI base units: [v] = m s⁻¹, [T] = kg m s⁻², [μ] = kg m⁻¹. For kgᵃ⁺ᵇ mᵃ⁻ᵇ s⁻²ᵃ = m¹ s⁻¹, −2a = −1 ⇒ a = 0.5 and b = −0.5, so v = √(T/μ). With μ = 3 × 10⁻³ = 0.003 kg m⁻¹, v = √(48 / 0.003) = 126 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds a = 1/2, b = −1/2, converts μ to 0.003 kg m⁻¹, and obtains v = 126 m s⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Deduces v = √(T/μ) correctly but forgets to convert μ from g m⁻¹ into kg m⁻¹ (off by √1000).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a = 1, b = −1 (computing T/μ with units m² s⁻²) without taking the square root required by dimensional homogeneity.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the dimensional ratio to √(μ/T), yielding s m⁻¹ instead of m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Dimensional analysis of a tensioned overhead catenary wire shows that mechanical pulse speed obeys v = Tᵃ μᵇ (unit prefactor), where T is axial tension and μ is mass per unit length. Field sensors record T = 64 N ± 1.5 N on a conductor of μ = 5 g m⁻¹ ± 0.15 g m⁻¹. What is the percentage uncertainty in the wave speed v deduced from dimensional homogeneity?
items.workedSolution: Dimensional homogeneity gives v = T^(1/2) μ^(−1/2). Hence %Δv = ½(%ΔT) + ½(%Δμ) = 0.5(1.5/64 + 0.15/5) × 100% = 2.67%.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Sums %ΔT + %Δμ without multiplying by the 1/2 power factor from the square-root exponents.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the percentage uncertainties because μ appears in the denominator of √(T/μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the combined percentage uncertainty by 2 instead of 1/2 for a square-root power.

items.stem: On a vertical Hooke's-law stand, the pointer of a helical coil spring reads x₁ = 12 mm ± 0.5 mm when unloaded and x₂ = 57 mm ± 0.5 mm under a calibrated load F = 18 N ± 0.4 N. Using Δ(x₂ − x₁) = Δx₁ + Δx₂, what is the percentage uncertainty in the spring constant k = F / (x₂ − x₁)?
items.workedSolution: Extension e = x₂ − x₁ = 57 − 12 = 45 mm with absolute uncertainty Δe = Δx₁ + Δx₂ = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1 mm. Thus %Δk = (%ΔF) + (%Δe) = (0.4/18 + 1/45) × 100% = 4.44%.

markScheme.criterion: Finds e = 45 mm, Δe = 1 mm, and obtains %Δk = 4.44%.

items.stem: During calibration of a railway buffer spring scale, a technician records datum position x₁ = 14 mm ± 0.8 mm before loading and x₂ = 74 mm ± 0.8 mm when axial force F = 36 N ± 0.5 N is applied. What is the absolute uncertainty Δk in the spring constant expressed in N m⁻¹?

markScheme.criterion: Combines Δe = 2Δx with ΔF/F + Δe/e to obtain Δk = 24.3 N m⁻¹.

items.stem: A glaciology instrument sled of mass 10 kg glides along horizontal frictionless ice at initial speed 1.5 m s⁻¹ when a winch cable applies a constant tension of 24 N angled at 60° above the horizontal for 4 s (sled remains in contact with the ice). What horizontal distance does the body travel during the 4 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Horizontal force F_x = 24 cos(60°) = 12 N, so a_x = F_x / m = 1.2 m s⁻². Using s = ut + ½a_x t² = (1.5)(4) + 0.5(1.2)(4)² = 15.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves F cos 60° to get a_x = 1.2 m s⁻² and obtains s = 15.6 m.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the full cable tension F/m without resolving along the horizontal direction of motion.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the initial-velocity displacement term ut.

markScheme.criterion: Finds a_x = 1.6 m s⁻² via F cos 36.87° / m and obtains v = 14.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses s = ut − ½gt² with g = 9.81 m s⁻² to obtain 21.2 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses +g instead of −g when initial velocity is upward, adding ½gt² to ut.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of 1/2 in the gravitational displacement term −½gt².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the motion as release from rest and omits the upward initial-velocity term ut.

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the mean vertical velocity u − ½gt rather than the instantaneous velocity u − gt.

items.stem: In a sports-engineering impact canon test, a ball of mass 0.06 kg strikes a rigid force plate normally at +15 m s⁻¹ and rebounds straight back along the same line at speed 12 m s⁻¹ (final velocity −12 m s⁻¹) after a contact duration of 5 ms. markScheme.criterion: Computes |Δp| = m(u + v_reb) and divides by 0.005 s to obtain 324 N.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts speed magnitudes m(u − v_reb)/Δt instead of accounting for velocity reversal m(u + v_reb)/Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by contact time in milliseconds without converting ms to seconds (off by 10³).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the impulse magnitude |Δp| in N s and forgets to divide by contact time Δt.

items.stem: In a chemical-process storage column (g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹ exact), a diaphragm gauge sits at depth h = 15 m ± 0.8 m below the free surface of a liquid of density ρ = 900 kg m⁻³ ± 15 kg m⁻³. What is the absolute uncertainty Δp in the hydrostatic gauge pressure in pascals?

items.stem: Using a digital micrometer, a student measures the diameter of a cylindrical constantan wire as d = 0.4 mm ± 0.01 mm while hanging a calibrated tensile load F = 32 N ± 0.8 N from it. What is the tensile stress σ in the wire in pascals?
items.workedSolution: Cross-sectional area A = πd²/4 = π(0.4 × 10⁻³)² / 4 = 1.26 × 10⁻⁷ m². Tensile stress σ = F / A = 4F / (πd²) = 2.55 × 10⁸ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Uses A = πd²/4 in m² to obtain σ = 2.55 × 10⁸ Pa.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses A = πd² instead of A = πd²/4 (treating diameter d as if it were radius r, off by a factor of 4).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides force by circumference πd instead of cross-sectional area πd²/4.

items.stem: In a spacecraft shunt-regulator test, a ceramic load resistor rated at R = 15 Ω ± 0.4 Ω operates with terminal p.d. V = 12 V ± 0.4 V. What is the absolute uncertainty ΔP in the dissipated electrical power in watts?
items.workedSolution: Nominal power P = V² / R = 12² / 15 = 9.60 W. Fractional uncertainty ΔP/P = 2(0.4/12) + (0.4/15) = 0.0933, giving ΔP = 0.896 W.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates P = V²/R and multiplies by 2(ΔV/V) + (ΔR/R) to obtain 0.896 W.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses ΔV/V + ΔR/R without doubling ΔV/V for V².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts ΔR/R from 2(ΔV/V) in the quotient V²/R.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (ΔV)² / ΔR directly instead of propagating fractional uncertainties.

items.workedSolution: Convert to SI base units: m = 34.4 × 10⁻³ = 0.0344 kg and L = 2.5 × 10⁻² = 0.025 m. Volume V = L³ = (0.025)³ m³. Bulk density ρ = m / L³ = 2.20 × 10³ kg m⁻³.

options.distractorRationale: Applies the centimetre prefix 10⁻² once rather than cubing it to (10⁻²)³ = 10⁻⁶ when converting cm³ to m³.
